assumptions: Assay sensitivity for capture and particle counting is sufficient to detect short-interval exposure in lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa.
Ex vivo microglia-like cytokine assays are sensitive and specific to detect modulation induced by captured material eluates.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal studies report functional effects but lack orthogonal intact-EV exposure verification; MISEV2023 recommends linking protected EV-associated cargo to function. Demonstrating that only material with an orthogonal intact-EV signature produces a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS modulation would support a mechanism-linked potency attribute and justify pursuing an EV-enriched drug substance rather than an undefined secretome.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Presence/absence and reproducible magnitude of ex vivo cytokine modulation correlated with in vivo orthogonal intact-EV evidence (capture-positive + particle co-localization) and abolished by membrane-disruption.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected mechanism-linked potency
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A mechanism-linked attribute that requires orthogonal intact-EV verification to predict short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation; links identity to potency per MISEV recommendations.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High: requires in vivo→ex vivo bridging data to support causal link.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed ex vivo modulation could result from soluble co-isolates that reach CNS compartments independently of intact EVs or from administration/dosing differences rather than intact-EV presence.
edges.missing_experiment: Orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment comparing capture-positive, membrane-intact material versus membrane-disrupted and capture-depleted controls with short-interval tissue sampling.
edges.uncertainty: High: rodent efficacy and MISEV support the need for orthogonal linkage but do not demonstrate an in vivo→ex vivo causal bridge; inference that intact-EV exposure is necessary for short-interval ex vivo modulation requires empirical testing.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect in vivo exposure could arise from assay insensitivity or labeling artifacts rather than absence of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: A matched intact-EV verification assay in short-interval in vivo samples concurrent with ex vivo functional readout.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: limited large-animal biodistribution after intranasal dosing suggests delivery barriers that could confound potency linkage, but the result may reflect formulation/labeling differences.

nodes.statement: An orthogonally defined intact-EV signature (capture-positive, particle-peak co-localization, detergent/protease-sensitive) identifies a membrane-protected EV fraction in conditioned medium.

If an administered preparation contains the orthogonal intact-EV signature and intact-EV exposure in nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa compartments is verifiable in vivo, then a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation will be observed from tissue-derived microglia-like cells.

If the administered preparation lacks the intact-EV signature, or the captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, then the short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation will be absent or qualitatively different.

competing_explanations: Bioactivity observed in rodents may derive from soluble secretome components that penetrate nasal barriers independently of intact EVs.
Negative large-animal biodistribution may be due to procedural/labeling differences rather than lack of intact-EV delivery.
dependencies: Orthogonal intact-EV analytics must be operational and validated for low-biomass matrices
Sufficient conditioned-medium production from a characterized source-cell bank
design_question: Daily question: Does in vivo short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa exposure of an orthogonally verified, membrane-protected, capture-positive EV fraction causally enable a reproducible ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation that is lost when the same material is membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted?
expected_measurable_effect: Reproducible correlation across independent lots and animal cohorts: presence of orthogonal intact-EV evidence in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples (capture-positive + particle co-localization) predicts a reduction in ex vivo LPS-induced cytokine readouts from harvested microglia-like cells; membrane disruption of administered material abolishes both in vivo capture signal and ex vivo modulation.

experiment.assay: Integrated protocol: (A) characterize administered materials in vitro with orthogonal intact-EV workflow (density fractionation + particle counts + immuno-capture + detergent/protease protection); (B) intranasal administration to rodents with short post-dose interval followed by collection of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue; (C) orthogonal verification of intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissues (capture and particle counts); (D) prepare ex vivo tissue-derived microglia-like cells, apply standardized inflammatory challenge (LPS) and measure cytokine release with and without co-incubation with captured-fraction eluates; (E) compare cytokine responses across arms.
experiment.comparator: Four-arm comparison from the same conditioned-medium lot: (1) intact-EV-enriched preparation (capture-positive), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining), (3) intact-EV-enriched material treated with detergent + protease prior to administration (membrane-disrupted), (4) particle-count-matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in the ex vivo assay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions. In-assay viability/assay controls for tissue health.
dependencies: Availability of sufficient conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank and passage range
Validated immuno-capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation sensitivity for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval tissue/fluid collection
Laboratory capability to run both orthogonal capture and ex vivo inflammatory assays
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible linkage between in vivo orthogonal intact-EV verification and the ex vivo cytokine readout across replicates, or particle-count-matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent ex vivo effects, indicating activity is not intact-EV-associated.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome with respect to the tested short-term ex vivo inflammatory readout; revise product-definition toward secretome-centric strategy and deprioritize EV-specific potency attribute.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected fraction (verified by capture + detergent/protease sensitivity and particle-peak co-localization) is necessary for a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation following intranasal administration; particle-count-matched but capture-negative or membrane-disrupted material will not produce the same ex vivo modulation.
experiment.primary_readout: Magnitude and reproducibility of ex vivo cytokine modulation (e.g., reduction in LPS-induced IL-6/TNF-α) from tissue-derived microglia-like cells correlated with in vivo orthogonal evidence of intact-EV exposure (presence of capture-positive signal and particle co-localization in lavage/CSF/tissue).
experiment.question: Can an orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge show that only capture-positive, membrane-protected material produces a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal administration, independent of bulk particle counts?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from a single characterized source-cell lot processed to produce: (A) enriched small-EV preparation (SEC/UC) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium without EV enrichment (secretome-retaining)
Matched aliquots of capture-positive material treated with detergent + protease (membrane-disrupted) prior to administration
Particle-count instruments and reagents (NTA or TRPS)
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Assays for orthogonal in vivo verification: capture from nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory mucosa homogenates and particle counts

Short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory assay platform (acutely harvested rodent olfactory-bulb/olfactory-mucosa-adjacent tissue processed to isolate microglia-like cells; LPS challenge; cytokine readouts such as IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex)
Positive control materials: characterized small EVs (commercial or lab-validated) and dexamethasone for ex vivo assay
Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions
secondary_readouts: Co-localization metrics between particle-count peaks and capture-positive ELISA signal in administered material and in collected lavage/CSF fractions
Confirmation that captured material's activity is abolished by detergent + protease pre-treatment
Protein:particle ratios of administered materials and of captured fractions
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium preps and animal cohorts)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In multiple independent conditioned-medium lots and animal cohorts (n ≥ 3), only the arm where administered material is orthogonally verified as capture-positive and shows particle-peak co-localization produces a reproducible reduction in ex vivo inflammatory cytokine readout; this reduction is abolished when captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, and particle-count-matched capture-negative or secretome-retaining arms do not produce equivalent ex vivo modulation.

explicit_inferences: Inference: An orthogonal intact-EV signature is a necessary mechanistic prerequisite for short-interval in vivo→ex vivo inflammatory modulation rather than bulk particle counts alone.
Inference: If the hypothesis is supported, the intact-EV signature can be used as a candidate potency-linked product-identity attribute and a manufacturing/process gate.
falsification_criteria: Failure across independent replicates: no reproducible linkage between in vivo orthogonal intact-EV verification and the ex vivo cytokine readout (i.e., capture-positive verification does not predict ex vivo modulation), or particle-count-matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent ex vivo effects.
human_decisions_required: Select source-cell lot(s) and passage window for the bridging experiment
Approve short-interval sampling schedule and animal cohort sizes
Approve choice of ex vivo inflammatory assay and cytokine endpoints
manufacturability_assessment: If supported, fractionation and downstream processing must be adjusted to preserve the orthogonal intact-EV signature; this will direct scalable fractionation, TFF envelope definition, and formulation compatibility testing per MISEV guidance.
manufacturing_rationale: If intact-EV-associated bioactivity is required for short-interval ex vivo modulation, then CMC should prioritize fractionation and processing steps that preserve the orthogonal intact-EV signature and adopt it as a release/lot-consistency gate per MISEV guidance.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal capture + particle-count verification in administered material and short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples, combined with ex vivo cytokine readouts from harvested tissue microglia-like cells; include membrane-disruption controls (detergent + protease/RNase) and particle-count-matched capture-depleted arms.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis is novel because it proposes an orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment that directly tests whether an orthogonally verified, membrane-protected, capture-positive EV fraction—rather than bulk particle counts or secretome components— is necessary for a short-interval CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal dosing. Prior program hypotheses focused on in vitro fractionation, source-senescence, fractionation workflows, process sensitivity, or cargo fingerprinting but did not propose the specific in vivo→ex vivo discriminating experiment that simultaneously verifies in vivo intact-EV exposure and tests functional consequence ex vivo.
principal_risks: Assay insensitivity for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples may produce false negatives.
Short-interval sampling window may miss transient exposure.
Ex vivo assay may not reflect in vivo therapeutic-relevant mechanisms or longer-term outcomes.
proposed_potency_relationship: If supported, the intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity will serve as a qualitative potency gate: capture-positive, particle-peak co-localizing fractions that lose activity after detergent+protease treatment indicate EV-associated potency and will be required for lot acceptance for potency-linked claims.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, adopt a mechanism-linked potency gate: an intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity (co-localizing with particle peaks, capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive) that predicts a short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal administration and serves as a potency-linked product-identity attribute.
title: Hypothesis: A membrane-protected, intact-EV-associated fraction is necessary for short-interval in vivo→ex vivo inflammatory modulation after intranasal dosing
